source.title: Not All Language Model Features Are One-Dimensionally Linear
source.authors: Joshua Engels; Eric J. Michaud; Isaac Liao; Wes Gurnee; Max Tegmark

page_placements.theme: Multi-dimensional (circular or manifold) features are fragmented by unit-level analyses

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies multidimensional SAE features and their causal use, not whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. Its findings concern a related representation construct, so they do not test any listed version of neuron polysemanticity.
record.gate_note: The paper reports multidimensional feature discoveries and interventions on circular representations; these are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]. It does not measure mixed responses of individual neurons. Task accuracy and circuit/EVR analyses are not included because they do not measure the claim's neuron-level subject.
record.test_reason: The paper studies multi-dimensional SAE features (circles for days, months, years) in GPT-2, Mistral 7B and Llama 3 8B. It never measures individual neuron selectivity, the share of polysemantic neurons, their causes, or how they vary by architecture or measurement. It proposes a multi-dimensional superposition hypothesis but does not test it against neuron polysemanticity. Its findings concern a related construct, feature geometry, and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors argue that some LM features are irreducibly multi-dimensional, such as circular day and month features found via SAE clustering and causally used in calendar arithmetic. They frame this as a refinement of the one-dimensional linear representation hypothesis, propose a multi-dimensional superposition hypothesis, and call their evidence preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE dictionary-element clustering, PCA projections, statistical irreducibility indices, and activation subspace interventions on language models; it does not use the original neuron visualization method or test SoLU.
record.method_sensitivity: For Mistral SAE clustering, the days-of-week cluster was not found when the similarity threshold was too low or too high; an intermediate threshold regime made it identifiable. Varying k had minimal effect. The circular-intervention effect also varies across layers, with the paper reporting it is strongest in early layers.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE clusters reconstruct circular representations of days, months and years in GPT-2 layer 7, and of days and months in Mistral 7B layer 8. Mistral also shows weekend and season regions on these circles. The days cluster scores Mϵ=0.475 and S=0.95.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some language-model features are irreducibly multi-dimensional, e.g. circular representations of ordered time concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: In Mistral 7B and Llama 3 8B, intervening on the circular subspace of the α token nearly matches patching the whole layer in early layers on weekday and month arithmetic. The SAE-plane probe transfers across layers better than a PCA probe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circular multi-dimensional representations are causally used in modular-arithmetic-like computations in LLMs.

record.problems: The authors describe the findings as preliminary and say it is unclear why they found few interpretable multidimensional features. They note that clustering may miss features, higher-dimensional structures may be harder to find, and the reducibility definitions are statistical and softened in practice. Intervention plots report 96% error bars, but many per-layer values are presented only graphically.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant neuron-polysemanticity results were reported. Other task-accuracy, patching, and EVR results were left out where they do not measure neuron responses or the related multidimensional-feature findings cataloged here.

untested.parts: Vision-model neurons that respond to unrelated inputs; no image models are studied.
Share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens; only SAE dictionary elements and residual activations are analysed.
Whether superposition causes neuron polysemanticity; superposition is assumed and extended theoretically (Hypothesis 2, Appendix A) but not tested against neurons.
Dependence on activation function, architecture or regularization.
Measurement dependence of neuron polysemanticity. The clustering threshold sensitivity (Fig. 16) concerns SAE clusters, not neurons.

record.verdict_notes: Neurons are never the unit of analysis. Superposition appears only as an assumed framework extended theoretically, so it should not be counted as a test of V3. Note that the r1 locator, Figure 2, uses PCA components 2–3 of the cluster.

versions.untested_parts: Individual neurons in image classifiers and their responses to unrelated image inputs.
The prevalence of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts in language models.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons.
Polysemantic neurons arising from initialization, regularization, or noise without capacity pressure.
Changes in the share of polysemantic neurons across architectures, activations, or regularization, and any performance tradeoff.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons have one shared feature or related jobs rather than unrelated mixtures.
Whether neuron polysemanticity depends on activation range examined or explanation scoring.

relation.reason: Discusses and restates the superposition hypothesis (Hypothesis 2) behind V3 but does not test polysemantic neurons; the word polysemantic never appears.

tranche.reason: Studies multi-dimensional SAE features (circles); never measures neuron selectivity, polysemantic neuron share, causes, or measurement dependence.

source_check.notes: All six rows match the text; they are SAE feature-space findings, not neuron measurements. The statement's 0.475/0.95 are rounded from 0.4750/0.9506. The Fig 2 days cluster is the GPT-2 one, even though the statement mentions it right after Mistral.
